supporting_observations.claim: The alerted periodic HTTPS activity is associated with C:\Program Files\CaseBinder\casebinderupd.exe, which the inventory identifies as the approved CaseBinder updater. The updater started under noah.kim at 13:39:01 and initiated a connection through the proxy shortly afterward.

The proxy logged repeated HTTPS CONNECT tunnels to update.casebinder.com, with corresponding endpoint network events attributed to the same updater process. The observed connections run from 13:39:30 through 14:09:02 at roughly five-minute intervals, consistent with the approved updater's inventory description.
The updater process exited at 14:09:36, shortly after its last observed connection in this sequence.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records identify the CONNECT destination and tunnel byte counts, but do not show the contents transferred through these updater tunnels.
The available records do not provide a file hash or signature verification for the updater executable; its path and process identity alone do not prove its integrity.
claims_not_established: The contents or safety of data exchanged within the CaseBinder HTTPS tunnels are not established by these records.
The records do not establish whether any updater response caused a file or configuration change.
unrelated_findings: Noah.kim's browser accessed docs.google.com and Google document resources. The inventory says no cloud-storage or file-sharing services other than Microsoft 365/OneDrive are approved; assess this separately from the CaseBinder alert. (T176-00085, T176-00086, T176-00090, T176-00091, T176-00092, T176-00093, T176-00094, T176-00095, T176-00104)

The greta.lund account obtained Kerberos tickets from WS-NKIM-01 and then logged on to FILE-MAP-01 from that workstation. This account/workstation activity is separate from the alerted HTTPS connections and warrants separate validation. (T176-00278, T176-00279, T176-00282)
